def class_setup(cls, request, android_hpx_flow_setup ,load_printers_session):

    cls.hpx_shortcuts = cls.fc.fd[FLOW_NAMES.HPX_SHORTCUTS]
    cls.fc.hpx = True
    logging.info("Starting Test Suite 01 for HPX Add Shortcuts")

def test_01_verify_the_screen_when_user_clicks_on_the_create_your_own_shortcut_arrow_button_in_add_new_shortcuts_screen_C46(self):
        """
        Verify the screen.
        TestRails -> https://hp-testrail.external.hp.com/index.php?/cases/view/46
        """
        self.fc.reset_app()
        self.fc.flow_load_home_screen(skip_value_prop=False)
        self.hpx_printer_details.click_add_device_btn()
        self.printers.search_printer_by_ip(self.p.ipAddress)
        self.hpx_printer_details.click_printer_device_card()
        self.hpx_printer_details.click_shortcuts_tile(raise_e=False)
        assert self.hpx_shortcuts.verify_shortcuts_screen_title()
        self.hpx_shortcuts.click_add_new_shortcut_btn()
        assert self.hpx_shortcuts.verify_add_new_shortcut_screen_title()

automation_scripts_rules.description: Test Setup and Precondition Handling Rule

THEN: These should be handled by test framework setup rather than explicit test method code

automation_scripts_rules.applies_to: All test cases with multiple automation script lines
rule_definition: WHEN: Test case has multiple explicit automation script lines (like Lines 1, 2, 3 in C47)
THEN: These must be executed in exact sequential order without skipping or reordering

IMPLEMENTATION: Each line represents a discrete step that depends on previous step completion. Line 1 (click action) must complete before Line 2 (back button), which must complete before Line 3 (verification). Include wait/confirmation steps between actions.

automation_scripts_rules.applies_to: Test cases that verify popup or dialog appearance after user action
rule_definition: WHEN: Test involves triggering popup/dialog and verifying its content
THEN: Must implement two-step pattern: trigger action + separate verification

IMPLEMENTATION: Step 1: Execute action that triggers popup (click_cancel_shortcut_go_back_btn). Step 2: Verify popup appears with expected content (verify_cancel_this_shortcut_title). Never combine action and verification in single method. Allow time for popup animation/rendering.

automation_scripts_rules.applies_to: All test case correlations between manual steps and automation scripts
rule_definition: WHEN: Creating correlation mapping for any test case
THEN: Every manual test step AND expected result must have corresponding correlation entry

IMPLEMENTATION: Include all numbered steps (1-7 in C47) plus expected result as separate correlation entry. Even implicit/framework-handled steps must be documented. No gaps allowed. Ensures complete traceability from manual test to automation implementation.

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Prerequisite Navigation Validation Rule
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: When test steps reference prerequisites or prior navigation steps (steps 1-N) that are not explicitly tested but required for test execution, an implicit step must be created to validate the target screen state before proceeding with actual test actions
application_criteria: Test step description contains phrases like 'Prerequisites from steps', 'Ensure user is on', 'Navigate to', or references prior setup steps
The implicit step must validate the expected screen/state is reached before executing the actual test steps
Must use assertion-based validation methods to confirm screen title, elements, or state

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Purpose-Based Validation Rule

application_criteria: The supporting step validates the primary expected result stated in custom_expected field
Must be distinct from explicit test step validations but may use the same validation method
Should be labeled as 'Supporting Step – Purpose of Test Case Validation' to distinguish from regular test steps
Provides redundancy and clarity for test case intent
automation_scripts_rules.automation_pattern: assert self.<page_object>.verify_<expected_outcome>() where expected_outcome aligns with the custom_expected field
automation_scripts_rules.example_from_test_case: Supporting Step – Purpose of Test Case Validation: Verify Add New Shortcut screen title is displayed maps to assert self.hpx_shortcuts.verify_add_new_shortcut_title() to validate the expected outcome 'User should be redirected to the Add Shortcut screen'
mandatory_intermediary_breakdown: Access the page object instance for the screen being validated
Execute the verification method to locate the element that confirms the expected outcome
Assert that the retrieved value is displayed and matches the expected outcome to validate test case purpose
automation_scripts_rules.compliance_requirement: Every test case must include at least one supporting step that directly validates the custom_expected field value, ensuring traceability between test intent and automation validation

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Direct Test Step to Script Line Mapping Rule
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: Each explicit test step from custom_steps must map to exactly one automation script line, maintaining clear traceability and ensuring no test step is omitted or combined without justification
application_criteria: Each numbered step in custom_steps (e.g., Step 6, Step 7, Step 8) must have a corresponding mapped_script_line
The mapping must preserve the sequential order of test steps
Action steps map to method calls without assertions; verification steps map to assertion statements
No test step should be skipped unless explicitly marked as implicit or supporting
automation_scripts_rules.automation_pattern: Action steps: self.<page_object>.<action_method>() | Verification steps: assert self.<page_object>.verify_<validation_target>()
automation_scripts_rules.example_from_test_case: Step 6: Click on the back button maps to self.hpx_shortcuts.click_cancel_shortcut_go_back_btn() | Step 8: Verify the screen maps to assert self.hpx_shortcuts.verify_add_new_shortcut_title()
mandatory_intermediary_breakdown: For action steps: Access page object, locate element using locator strategy, execute action method
For verification steps: Wait for state/transition if needed, execute verification method, assert returned value matches expected result
automation_scripts_rules.compliance_requirement: Correlation array must contain entries for all explicit test steps with no gaps in step numbering, ensuring complete test coverage and audit trail

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Granular Action Decomposition Rule
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: Every automation script line must be decomposed into 2-4 granular intermediary steps that explicitly describe the technical actions performed, including page object access, element location strategy, method execution, and validation logic
application_criteria: Each mapped_script_line in correlation must have a corresponding entry in intermediary_steps array
Intermediary steps must be technically explicit, describing object initialization, locator usage, method calls, and assertions
For assertion-based steps, must include wait/transition handling where applicable
Steps must be ordered sequentially to reflect actual execution flow
automation_scripts_rules.automation_pattern: Action decomposition: [Access page object, Locate element with locator strategy, Execute method] | Verification decomposition: [Wait for state if needed, Execute verification method, Assert expected value]
automation_scripts_rules.example_from_test_case: self.hpx_shortcuts.click_cancel_shortcut_go_back_btn() breaks down to: ['Access the hpx_shortcuts page object instance', 'Locate the back button element on the Add Shortcut screen using the defined locator strategy', 'Execute the click_cancel_shortcut_go_back_btn() method to perform the click action on the back button element']
mandatory_intermediary_breakdown: Step 1: Always specify page object instance access or initialization
Step 2: Describe element location mechanism (locator strategy, wait conditions)
Step 3: Detail the method execution and its purpose
Step 4 (if applicable): For assertions, specify the validation logic and expected outcome comparison
automation_scripts_rules.compliance_requirement: All intermediary_steps entries must contain between 2-4 granular steps; no single-step entries allowed; each step must be a complete sentence describing a discrete technical action

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Consistent Method Naming and Reuse Rule
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: When the same UI element or action is referenced multiple times across test steps, the same automation method must be reused to ensure consistency, reduce maintenance overhead, and enforce DRY principles
application_criteria: Identical or semantically equivalent actions on the same element must use the same method name
Method names must follow naming convention: <action>_<element_identifier>_<element_type> for actions, verify_<validation_target> for verifications
If the same button/element appears in different contexts (e.g., screen vs popup), the method may be reused if the locator strategy is context-aware
automation_scripts_rules.automation_pattern: Reuse pattern: self.<page_object>.<consistent_method_name>() across multiple test steps
automation_scripts_rules.example_from_test_case: Both Step 6 and Step 7 use self.hpx_shortcuts.click_cancel_shortcut_go_back_btn() even though contexts differ (Add Shortcut screen vs popup), demonstrating method reuse with context-aware locator handling

Locator strategy description must indicate how the method handles different contexts if applicable
automation_scripts_rules.compliance_requirement: Automation architects must review correlation mappings to identify opportunities for method reuse; duplicate method names for identical actions are prohibited unless justified by technical constraints

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Explicit Assertion Validation Rule
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: All verification and validation steps must use explicit assertion statements (assert keyword) with verification methods that return boolean or comparable values, ensuring test failures are clearly identified and reported
application_criteria: Any test step containing 'Verify', 'Validate', 'Check', 'Ensure', or 'Confirm' must map to an assertion statement
Verification methods must return values that can be asserted (boolean, string match, element presence)
Assertions must include meaningful failure context through method naming (e.g., verify_add_new_shortcut_title clearly indicates what is being validated)

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Test Step Type Identification Rule
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: All test steps must be classified into one of four types: Implicit Steps (prerequisites/navigation), Explicit Steps (numbered test actions), Supporting Steps (purpose validation), or Verification Steps (expected outcome checks), with appropriate labeling and handling
application_criteria: Implicit Steps: Labeled with 'Implicit Step – Required for Test Execution' prefix, validate prerequisites
Explicit Steps: Retain original step numbering (Step N), map directly to test actions
Supporting Steps: Labeled with 'Supporting Step – Purpose of Test Case Validation' prefix, validate test case objective
Verification Steps: Subset of Explicit Steps containing validation actions, use assertion pattern
automation_scripts_rules.automation_pattern: Implicit: assert self.<page_object>.verify_<prerequisite_state>() | Explicit Action: self.<page_object>.<action_method>() | Explicit Verification: assert self.<page_object>.verify_<outcome>() | Supporting: assert self.<page_object>.verify_<test_purpose>()
automation_scripts_rules.example_from_test_case: Implicit: 'Implicit Step – Required for Test Execution: Navigate to Add Shortcut screen' | Explicit Action: 'Step 6: Click on the back button' | Explicit Verification: 'Step 8: Verify the screen' | Supporting: 'Supporting Step – Purpose of Test Case Validation: Verify Add New Shortcut screen title'
mandatory_intermediary_breakdown: Step classification must be determined during test case analysis phase
Each classification type has specific intermediary step patterns (implicit requires navigation confirmation, supporting requires purpose alignment)
Classification must be reflected in test_step field labeling
automation_scripts_rules.compliance_requirement: Every test case must contain at least one implicit step (if prerequisites exist), all explicit steps from custom_steps, at least one supporting step, and at least one verification step; correlation array must reflect this classification

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Page Object Model Enforcement Rule
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: All automation scripts must follow Page Object Model (POM) pattern where UI interactions are encapsulated in page object classes, and test scripts only call page object methods, ensuring separation of concerns and maintainability
application_criteria: All mapped_script_lines must reference page object instances (self.<page_object_name>)
Direct element locators or UI interaction code must not appear in test scripts
Page object methods must be named descriptively to indicate the action and target element
Page object instance must be initialized before use (covered in intermediary steps)
automation_scripts_rules.automation_pattern: self.<page_object_instance>.<method_name>() where page_object_instance represents a screen/component and method_name describes the action/verification
automation_scripts_rules.example_from_test_case: All script lines use self.hpx_shortcuts.<method>() pattern, where hpx_shortcuts is the page object for the shortcuts functionality
mandatory_intermediary_breakdown: First intermediary step for each test script step must reference page object access or initialization
Locator strategy details belong in intermediary steps, not in the script line itself
Method execution step must clearly state which page object method is being called
automation_scripts_rules.compliance_requirement: Zero tolerance for direct element interaction in test scripts; all UI interactions must be abstracted through page object methods; code reviews must enforce POM compliance

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Explicit Wait Strategy Rule
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: For steps involving screen transitions, popup appearances, or dynamic content loading, intermediary steps must include explicit wait conditions to ensure element availability and prevent flaky test execution
application_criteria: Steps following navigation actions, button clicks that trigger transitions, or popup interactions must include wait conditions
Wait conditions must be described in intermediary steps (e.g., 'Wait for popup screen to be visible and interactable')
Verification steps after transitions must include 'Wait for screen transition to complete' before assertion

Add explicit wait step as first intermediary action after transition trigger
Specify wait condition type (visibility, interactability, element presence, state change)
automation_scripts_rules.compliance_requirement: All steps involving UI state changes must include explicit wait conditions in intermediary steps; implicit waits alone are insufficient for compliance-driven automation

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Validation Steps Must Include Purpose-Explicit Supporting Steps

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Automation Script Execution Order Must Strictly Follow Test Case Logic Flow
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: The sequence of automation script calls must exactly mirror the logical flow defined in test case steps, including all intermediary validations and state transitions. automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Missing Explicit Verifications Must Be Documented as Implicit Gaps

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Each Intermediary Step Must Represent Single Atomic Operation

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: All UI Element Interactions Must Follow Locate-Verify-Act-Wait Pattern
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: Every interaction with UI elements must follow the standardized four-phase pattern: 1.Locate element using predefined locator strategy, 2.Verify element state (visible, enabled, clickable), 3.Execute action on element, 4.Wait for resulting state change or transition completion. automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: All Assertions Must Include Failure Handling and Descriptive Messages
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: Every assertion in automation scripts must include explicit failure handling logic and descriptive error messages that identify the specific validation that failed, expected vs. actual values, and context of the failure. Silent assertion failures are prohibited.
automation_scripts_rules.applicability: All assert statements and verification methods in automation scripts
automation_scripts_rules.implementation_pattern: assert condition, f'Descriptive message: Expected {expected}, Actual {actual}, Context: {context}' OR try-except with explicit failure logging
automation_scripts_rules.example_from_context: Step 7b: assert self.hpx_shortcuts.verify_cancel_this_shortcut_title() with failure handling for title verification
validation_criteria: Assertion must include descriptive failure message
Expected and actual values must be logged on failure
Context of assertion (which step, which screen) must be provided
Assertion failures must be caught and logged appropriately
automation_scripts_rules.consequences_of_violation: Cryptic test failure messages, inability to diagnose failures without debugging, poor test maintainability, increased failure investigation time

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Test Execution State Readiness Must Be Validated Before Critical Steps
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: Before executing critical test steps (especially those involving destructive actions, confirmations, or state transitions), the test must validate that all prerequisite conditions are met and the application is in the expected state. State validation checkpoints must be implemented at test boundaries and before irreversible actions.
automation_scripts_rules.applicability: All test cases with prerequisites, state dependencies, or destructive actions
automation_scripts_rules.example_from_context: Implicit step validates: prerequisite navigation completed, HPX app launched, navigation path verified, cancel dialog displayed, test execution state ready
validation_criteria: Prerequisite completion must be validated before test execution
Application state must match expected state before critical actions
Navigation path must be verified before dependent steps
State validation failures must halt test execution with clear error
automation_scripts_rules.consequences_of_violation: Test execution in incorrect state, cascading failures, false negatives, inability to isolate root cause, unreliable test results

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Automation Script Functions Must Be Modular and Reusable Across Test Cases
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: All automation script functions must be designed for reusability across multiple test cases. Functions should accept parameters for variable inputs, avoid hard-coded test-specific values, and implement single responsibility. Common workflows must be extracted into shared utility functions.
automation_scripts_rules.applicability: All automation script function definitions and page object methods
automation_scripts_rules.implementation_pattern: def reusable_action(self, param1, param2, expected_state): [parameterized implementation] usable across multiple test contexts
automation_scripts_rules.example_from_context: Functions like click_cancel_shortcut_yes_cancel_btn() and verify_cancel_this_shortcut_title() are reusable across any test case involving shortcut cancellation
validation_criteria: Functions must accept parameters for variable inputs
No hard-coded test case-specific values in function body
Functions must implement single, well-defined responsibility
Common workflows must be extracted into shared utilities
automation_scripts_rules.consequences_of_violation: Code duplication, maintenance burden, inconsistent implementations, inability to scale automation, technical debt accumulation

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: All Automation Scripts Must Maintain Bidirectional Traceability to Test Cases
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: Every automation script must maintain clear, bidirectional traceability to source test cases through test case IDs, step references, and correlation documentation. Scripts must include comments referencing source test case steps, and correlation JSON must map every test step to corresponding automation code.

def test_06_verify_the_behavior_when_user_enables_the_print_destination_toggle_bar_in_add_shortcut_screen_C51(self):
        """
        Verify the behavior when user enables the print destination toggle bar.
        TestRails -> https://hp-testrail.external.hp.com/index.php?/cases/view/51
        """
        self.fc.reset_app()
        self.fc.flow_load_home_screen(skip_value_prop=False)
        self.hpx_printer_details.click_add_device_btn()
        self.printers.search_printer_by_ip(self.p.ipAddress)
        self.hpx_printer_details.click_printer_device_card()
        self.hpx_printer_details.click_shortcuts_tile(raise_e=False)
        assert self.hpx_shortcuts.verify_shortcuts_screen_title()
        self.hpx_shortcuts.click_add_new_shortcut_btn()
        assert self.hpx_shortcuts.verify_add_new_shortcut_screen_title()
        self.hpx_shortcuts.click_create_your_own_shortcut()
        self.hpx_shortcuts.click_edit_shortcut_print_toggle_btn()
        assert self.hpx_shortcuts.is_continue_btn_enabled(), "Continue button should be enabled after toggling print option"

automation_scripts_rules.description: One-to-Many Step Mapping for Application Launch
automation_scripts_rules.applies_to: Test steps involving complex initialization like 'Install and Launch the HPX app'
rule_definition: WHEN: A test step involves both installation/reset and launching of an application
THEN: Split the step into sub-steps (1a, 1b) where 1a handles reset/initialization and 1b handles loading/launching

IMPLEMENTATION: Step 1a → self.fc.reset_app() (clear application state, terminate sessions, reset to initial state), Step 1b → self.fc.flow_load_home_screen(skip_value_prop=False) (navigate through launch sequence, display value proposition, verify home screen ready)

automation_scripts_rules.description: Implicit Required Steps for Printer Setup
automation_scripts_rules.applies_to: Test cases involving printer interaction that require device setup
rule_definition: WHEN: Test case involves clicking on printer icon or accessing printer functionality
THEN: Include implicit steps for printer setup before the actual test steps

IMPLEMENTATION: Add 'Click add device button to initiate printer setup' → self.hpx_printer_details.click_add_device_btn() and 'Search and select printer by IP address' → self.printers.search_printer_by_ip(self.p.ipAddress) as required implicit steps

automation_scripts_rules.description: Supporting Validation Steps for Screen Navigation
automation_scripts_rules.applies_to: Test cases involving navigation between screens in shortcut management
rule_definition: WHEN: Test case navigates to shortcuts screen or add new shortcut screen
THEN: Include implicit supporting validation steps to verify screen display

IMPLEMENTATION: After navigation to shortcuts screen, add 'Verify shortcuts screen is displayed' → assert self.hpx_shortcuts.verify_shortcuts_screen_title(). After navigation to add new shortcut screen, add 'Verify add new shortcut screen is displayed' → assert self.hpx_shortcuts.verify_add_new_shortcut_screen_title()

automation_scripts_rules.applies_to: Test steps involving enabling/disabling toggle buttons or switches
rule_definition: WHEN: Test step involves enabling a toggle bar or switch
THEN: Implement toggle action followed by validation of resulting state

IMPLEMENTATION: For toggle action → use click method on toggle element (self.hpx_shortcuts.click_edit_shortcut_print_toggle_btn()), followed by validation step to verify expected state change and UI response

automation_scripts_rules.description: Screen Verification with Specific UI Element Validation
automation_scripts_rules.applies_to: Test steps with generic verification like 'Verify the screen'
rule_definition: WHEN: Test step requires screen verification after a toggle or configuration action
THEN: Implement specific UI element validation that confirms the action's effect

IMPLEMENTATION: Use assertion with descriptive error message to validate specific UI element state (assert self.hpx_shortcuts.is_continue_btn_enabled(), 'Continue button should be enabled after toggling print option')

automation_scripts_rules.description: Error Suppression for Optional Navigation Elements
automation_scripts_rules.applies_to: Navigation actions where element might not be immediately available
rule_definition: WHEN: Clicking on tiles or navigation elements that might have timing issues
THEN: Use error suppression parameter to handle graceful failures
IMPLEMENTATION: Include raise_e=False parameter in click methods for navigation elements (self.hpx_printer_details.click_shortcuts_tile(raise_e=False))

automation_scripts_rules.description: Mandatory Intermediary Steps for UI Interactions
automation_scripts_rules.applies_to: All UI interaction steps in automation scripts
rule_definition: WHEN: Implementing any UI interaction (click, toggle, navigation)
THEN: Include 5-6 intermediary steps covering element location, validation, interaction, and post-action verification
IMPLEMENTATION: 1) Locate element, 2) Verify element state, 3) Perform interaction, 4) Handle synchronization, 5) Validate result, 6) Optional: Handle viewport adjustments or error conditions
